title: An iterable range with steps
description:
Write `class Range implements Iterable<Integer>`:

- `Range.of(start, end)` and `Range.of(start, end, step)`: the numbers from `start` up to but not including `end`, going by `step` (default 1). A negative step counts down (to just above `end`). A step of 0 throws `IllegalArgumentException`.
- `iterator()` returns an object of a **private inner class** that walks the range; `next()` past the end throws `NoSuchElementException`.
- `size()` returns how many numbers the range contains (0 if it is empty).
- `toList()` returns the numbers as a `List<Integer>`.

```java
for (int n : Range.of(10, 0, -3)) System.out.print(n + " ");   // 10 7 4 1
```
hints: The inner class `Walker` can read `start`, `end` and `step` of the `Range` that created it directly: that is what makes it an inner class rather than a static one.
`hasNext()` depends on the direction: `next < end` when counting up, `next > end` when counting down. Writing `toList()` with a for-each over `this` reuses the iterator.
